extracted.intended_audience: aspiring nature writers and reflective personal-essay authors; general readers of Whitman-style prose
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing observational, nature-centered personal essays and field jottings that rely on sensory detail, fragmentary notes, and attention to ordinary scenes and interior life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take notes in the field / record contemporaneous observations
rubrics_metrics.description: Wherever I go, indeed, winter or summer, city or country, alone at home or traveling, I must take notes--(the ruling passion strong in age and disablement...)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jot down impressions on the spot; many passages are from 'hastily-written first notes.' Accept and use these immediate, unpolished jottings as the raw material for finished prose. (Printers may be vexed by the lack of consecutiveness, but these first notes are valuable.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose conducive places and seasons for composition
rubrics_metrics.description: I find the woods in mid-May and early June my best places for composition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek settings (woods, creek-banks, early summer mornings) that stimulate observation and mood. Sit on logs or stumps, rest on rails — the physical setting contributes to the material you gather.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make Nature the enduring subject and source
rubrics_metrics.description: After you have exhausted what there is in business, politics, conviviality, love, and so on... what remains? Nature remains; to bring out from their torpid recesses, the affinities of a man or woman with the open air...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Center writing on human affinities with the open air and nature's cycles; treat nature as the permanent wellspring after transient subjects are spent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rely on concrete sensory detail (sight, smell, sound, movement)
rubrics_metrics.description: The lights, perfumes, melodies--the blue birds, grass birds and robins, in every direction--the noisy, vocal, natural concert. For undertones, a neighboring wood-pecker tapping his tree, and the distant clarion of chanticleer. Then the fresh-earth smells--the colors, the delicate drabs and thin blues of the perspective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Populate scenes with precise sensory elements (color, smell, sound, tactile impressions, motion). Use these particulars to make the scene vivid rather than abstract generalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record ordinary people and interior character; favor intimate scenes
rubrics_metrics.description: To me the main interest I found... in the rank and file of the armies, both sides, and in those specimens amid the hospitals... points illustrating the latent personal character and eligibilities of these States...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give attention to everyday individuals, their personal reactions, and small interior moments; these human-scale glimpses often reveal deeper truths than grand narratives or official accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid relying only on official or sanitized narratives; capture the 'real' and unwritten
rubrics_metrics.description: The real war will never get in the books... its practicality, minutia; of deeds and passions, will never be even suggested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not restrict writing to formal histories or public faces. Seek and record the lurid interiors, hospital scenes, and messy human details that official accounts omit — these are often the essential truth of events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone down wants and tastes; make much of negatives and simple elements
rubrics_metrics.description: The trick is, I find, to tone your wants and tastes low down enough, and make much of negatives, and of mere daylight and the skies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt modest desires and attention to small, simple phenomena (daylight, sky, modest pleasures). Elevating the understated and negative spaces in experience can yield depth and calm in prose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embrace fragmentary, non-linear jottings as a compositional method
rubrics_metrics.description: There is little consecutiveness in dates. They run any time within nearly five or six years. Each was carelessly pencilled in the open air, at the time and place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept non-sequential notes and fragments; publish or assemble them as loosely connected memoranda. Fragmentary structure can be a deliberate method, not a flaw.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve ephemeral particulars and fleeting objects
rubrics_metrics.description: These cedar-apples last only a little while however, and soon crumble and fade. On my ramble afterward down by the creek I pluck'd one from its bush, and shall keep it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice and record transient things (short-lived fruits, a particular day's sky). Saving such ephemeral details in prose captures the temporality and richness of place.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use musicality, rhythm, and metaphor in prose
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there not a hint in it for a musical composition, of which it should be the back-ground? some bumble-bee symphony?... How it all nourishes, lulls me, in the way most needed;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listen for rhythms and harmonies in sounds and movements; allow musical metaphors and rhythmic phrasing to shape sentences and passages. Let prose sometimes function like music to evoke mood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Catalogue local flora and fauna to convey place and intimacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Trees I am familiar with here. Oaks, (many kinds--one sturdy old fellow...) Cedars plenty... Tulip trees... Sycamores... Beeches... Black-walnuts... Sassafras. ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use enumerations and lists of local species and features to build texture and authority about a place. Cataloguing can create intimacy and a sense of lived familiarity with the landscape.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observe and identify species and timing for authenticity
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you ever chance to hear the midnight flight of birds... I could make out the bobolink, tanager, Wilson's thrush, white-crown'd sparrow, and occasionally... the plover.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note specific species, behaviors, and seasonal timing (e.g., 'midnight flight of birds', cicada vs katydid, locust-song rhythms). Specific identification lends credibility and precision to natural description.
